events.title: Cerebras unveils CS-4 at SUPERNOVA 2026 — rack-scale 750 PFLOPS system on three WSE-3 Turbo wafers
events.title_zh: Cerebras 在 SUPERNOVA 2026 发布 CS-4——三片 WSE-3 Turbo 晶圆组成的机架级 750 PFLOPS 系统
events.published_at_note: Announced during the SUPERNOVA 2026 keynote (livestream from ~22:30Z, Aug 18); press release syndicated 2026-08-18. In-window. Independent coverage: StockTitan (2026-08-18) and live cerebras.ai homepage; search indexes had not caught up at scan time.
events.summary: At its SUPERNOVA 2026 event Cerebras unveiled CS-4, a rack-scale AI system built on three new WSE-3 Turbo wafers delivering 750 PFLOPS of AI compute. Claims: up to 2x faster than CS-3, up to 30x more tokens-per-second-per-user than leading GPU-based solutions, up to 10x better throughput per watt, 129.6 PB/s memory bandwidth, 7.2 Tb/s I/O, wafer-to-wafer latency as low as two microseconds. Introduces the modular Nexus Platform Architecture with pluggable Wafer-Scale Backpack and Direct Wafer Links, supporting models beyond 50 trillion parameters. First shipments expected this quarter.
events.why_it_matters: The first mainstream rack-scale wafer-stacking product: if the per-user latency and throughput-per-watt claims hold in independent benchmarks, it changes the economics of latency-sensitive inference (agents, interactive coding, voice) and pushes the frontier toward >50T-parameter dense serving. All figures are vendor 'up to' claims at announcement — verify before planning capacity.

events.update_2026_08_19: Independent analysis wave post-announcement: SemiAnalysis 'Cerebras's Next Generation CS-4: Fast Just Got Faster' (2026-08-18, coverage-gap recovery — published in the previous window but index-lag prevented capture) concludes CS-4 roughly doubles CS-3 performance mainly via increased power consumption, higher per-wafer clock frequency and rack-scale density rather than a new chip generation ('Double the Performance with Double the Power'); TNW frames it as Cerebras' first multi-wafer system with essentially faster-clocked WSE-3 silicon; TechTimes cites ~4,400 tokens/sec decode (~2x CS-3 token speed, ~6x system-level throughput) with no new silicon (same 5nm wafer, higher clocks); per-wafer figures cited: 44GB on-wafer SRAM, 250 PFLOPS, 43.2 PB/s memory bandwidth. Nexus Platform Architecture details: pluggable Wafer-Scale Backpack, RoCE v2, Direct Wafer Links. Hardware pricing still undisclosed; first-shipments-this-quarter reiterated by HPCwire/IBD/DataCenterDynamics. Also verified: SUPERNOVA 2026 produced no additional product/model announcements beyond CS-4 (investors newsroom + StockTitan CBRS feed checked 2026-08-20). Recommendation stays WATCH pending independent benchmarks and shipment evidence.

events.title: OpenAI Codex CLI 0.148.0 stable — session forking, async hooks that invoke MCP tools, built-in Amazon Bedrock provider
events.title_zh: OpenAI Codex CLI 0.148.0 稳定版——会话 fork、可调用 MCP 工具的异步 hooks、内置 Amazon Bedrock provider
events.published_at_note: GitHub stable release published 2026-08-18T22:26Z by github-actions. In-window.
events.summary: Codex CLI 0.148.0 (stable) adds: session forking via `codex exec fork` plus archive/restore of sessions from the TUI resume picker; markdown conversation export (`/export` to clipboard or file); prompt drafting during TUI startup; estimated thread credits/cost visible in `/status`, status lines and terminal titles; Amazon Bedrock Runtime as a built-in provider (AWS profile, region selection, GPT-5.6 routing); hooks can now run commands asynchronously and invoke MCP tools. Fixes: stale instructions after model switching; resumed sessions restore cwd and approval policy; reconnection through provider outages; MCP recovery after OAuth re-auth; sandbox restrictions now fail closed for denied/unreadable paths on Linux and Windows.
events.why_it_matters: Three engineering-relevant moves in one release: (1) session forking lands in the stable channel, extending Codex's multi-agent primitives from subagent spawning to exec-level branch/run-parallel workflows; (2) async hooks that can call MCP tools turn Codex into a programmable orchestration point; (3) a built-in Bedrock provider gives AWS shops a first-party path to Codex models with profile/region handling, and cost visibility (`/status` credits) closes a long-standing budgeting gap.

events.title: KV-Cache retention breaks rollback consistency in language agents (arXiv 2608.15939)
events.title_zh: KV-Cache 残留会破坏语言 agent 的回滚一致性（arXiv 2608.15939）
events.published_at_note: v1 submitted 2026-08-16 21:49:38 UTC; announced in the Tue, 18 Aug 2026 arXiv cs.CL digest (in-window). cs.CL. Authors: Guijia Zhang, Harry Yang (affiliations not stated on abstract page).
events.summary: Paper shows that 'logical' rollback in stateful language agents is not a real rollback: if the serving session retains key/value (KV) cache state after an aborted branch, the model keeps attending to supposedly discarded content. The authors formalize the missing guarantee as 'rollback consistency' (a full abort must restore the model's attended state, not merely the transcript), and demonstrate the flaw with a same-token/different-cache audit across seven open-weight model families (3.8B-36B) in real settings: the default Hugging Face Transformers cache-reuse path and LangGraph time-travel, where verified logical rollback still leaves stale KV; it also reproduces in an end-to-end session application. Stale KV alone flips a typed protected effect in 25 of 63 audited cells, with attacker tokens absent from all 63 served requests; rebuilding the cache closes every case. Proposed fix: transaction-local cache restoration at abort time (no global cache flush needed). Results claimed deterministic and reproducible from released artifacts.
events.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to anyone running agents with branch/reject/retry loops (LangGraph time-travel, tree-search agents, Claude Code-style forking): cross-session and subagent forks are only safe if the serving path actually rebuilds attention state. The failure is invisible at the application layer — audits must target the serving stack. Also a security channel: attacker-influenced content can persist in cache after logical removal. Simple mitigation: rebuild/restore cache at abort boundaries.
events.summary_zh: 论文证明 stateful language agent 中的「逻辑」回滚并不是真正的回滚：如果 serving 会话在分支被中止后保留 KV cache 状态，模型仍会 attend 到本应丢弃的内容。作者将缺失的保证形式化为「rollback consistency」（完全中止必须还原模型 attended 状态，而不仅是 transcript），并用 same-token/different-cache 审计在七个开源模型家族（3.8B–36B）上验证，场景包括真实路径：Hugging Face Transformers 默认 cache-reuse 和 LangGraph time-travel（已验证的逻辑回滚仍留下 stale KV），且在端到端会话应用中复现。仅 stale KV 就使 63 个审计单元中的 25 个翻转受保护效果，且 63 个实际请求中都看不到攻击者 token；重建 cache 后所有案例消除。修复方案：中止时做 transaction-local 的 cache 重建/还原（无需全局 flush）。结果声称确定性、可由已发布 artifacts 复现。
events.summary_en: Paper shows that 'logical' rollback in stateful language agents is not a real rollback: if the serving session retains key/value (KV) cache state after an aborted branch, the model keeps attending to supposedly discarded content. The authors formalize the missing guarantee as 'rollback consistency' (a full abort must restore the model's attended state, not merely the transcript), and demonstrate the flaw with a same-token/different-cache audit across seven open-weight model families (3.8B-36B) in real settings: the default Hugging Face Transformers cache-reuse path and LangGraph time-travel, where verified logical rollback still leaves stale KV; it also reproduces in an end-to-end session application. Stale KV alone flips a typed protected effect in 25 of 63 audited cells, with attacker tokens absent from all 63 served requests; rebuilding the cache closes every case. Proposed fix: transaction-local cache restoration at abort time (no global cache flush needed). Results claimed deterministic and reproducible from released artifacts.
events.why_it_matters_zh: 对任何在 agent 中使用分支/拒绝/重试循环的人（LangGraph time-travel、tree-search agent、Claude Code 式 forking）都直接相关：跨会话与 subagent fork 只有在 serving 路径真正重建注意力状态时才是安全的。该缺陷在应用层不可见——审计必须针对 serving 栈。同时这也是一个安全通道：受攻击者影响的内容可以在逻辑删除后残留在 cache 中。缓解方式简单：在中止边界重建/还原 cache。

The failure is invisible at the application layer — audits must target the serving stack. Also a security channel: attacker-influenced content can persist in cache after logical removal. Simple mitigation: rebuild/restore cache at abort boundaries.
